For node_handler, I'm including node assignments plus sample work at their node; laboratory_team sees lab assignments with expected sample types; dispatcher/administrator sees all journey work items mapped to pending/inProgress/completed by journey status, with history drawn from a timeline table filtered by entity.

Now I'm designing the audit_log table with actor, role, action, entity type/id, success flag, timestamp, and a jsonb details column, considering adding a related_sample_id column to simplify sample timeline lookups.

I'm adding a sample_ids array column to audit entries so sample timelines can query by containment, and defining the TimelineEntry shape with event id, action, actor, role, entity, success, timestamp, and details. I'll duplicate camelCase and snake_case fields across AuditEntry and SampleWorkItem for compatibility, and plan to log sign-ins and permission checks into the audit trail too.

Now I'm designing search_audit_trail with free-text filtering over action/entity/details, restricting access to dispatcher/admin roles while returning 403 otherwise. For realtime events, I'm sketching an events table with type, entity references, payload, audience, and a GET endpoint that upgrades to a websocket stream using a custom subprotocol for auth.

For idempotency, I'm planning a table keyed by user and idempotency key storing the original request hash and response, so repeated calls replay the stored result while mismatched requests with the same key return a 409 conflict, and I'll require this key for mutation endpoints like create_collection_request and ingest.

For conflicts, I'll run mutations inside transactions with row locks and translate Postgres serialization errors into a generic 409 concurrent_conflict response. For worker location tracking, I'm designing a sequence-based validation so each new location must have a strictly increasing sequence number per assignment, rejecting stale or out-of-order updates, and updating the sample's latest known location only when the reporting worker currently holds it.

Now I'm defining staleness rules based on a time threshold, then deciding how a sample's latest location is derived depending on whether its holder is a worker or a node, updating it on key lifecycle events like handoffs, sealing, and receipt. I'm also sketching the UI bootstrap endpoint's response shape and starting to lay out the permissions matrix by role.

Continuing the permissions matrix, I'm working through who can create users, configure locations and capacity, set availability, and initiate collection requests or ingest preseal samples — wrestling with the ingestion case since the rule seems to require the registrant to be the current physical holder, which would exclude admins.

For reading and progressing samples, I'm restricting to the four worker roles plus requester/dispatcher/admin based on ownership or assignment, scoping journey plans differently by role, and limiting accept/decline, collection and sealing, assignment progress updates, and location recording to the workers actually holding or assigned to that work.

Now I'm moving to frontend planning — a login page, an app shell with a role switcher and role-based navigation, and the requester flow starting with serviceability checks, new requests, and a sample list leading into a detailed sample view with status, location, timeline, and map.

Worker views need pending/in-progress/completed work queues with actions like accept, collect, seal, record location, and handoffs, plus node/lab-specific capacity and receipt forms. Dispatcher/admin needs a monitoring dashboard with live map, journey detail actions, disruption reporting, audit search, and admin screens for users, locations, connections, and sample types — I'll keep the UI functional with plain CSS rather than overengineering it.

Now I'm thinking through the Go backend layout — deciding between a deep internal package structure (config, db, httpapi, domain, ws) versus a flatter organization like store/app/api, or even just a single internal/server package with many files given the overall scope.

I'm settling on separate packages for config, db (pool/migrate/reset), model, geo (haversine), audit, events (hub+persistence), core (all the business services), and httpapi for handlers, with cmd/server as entry point. For migrations I'll use a single idempotent schema.sql with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, and reset support via dropping and recreating the public schema, triggered by a -reset flag on the server binary.

I also want the build script to compile both the Go binary and frontend, with reset falling back to building the binary if it's missing, plus startup seeding logic for an admin user from env vars and default sample types when none exist. Now I'm starting to write out the database schema, beginning with settings and users tables covering roles, qualifications, and certifications.

Defining more tables...

Still defining more tables...

Still designing more tables...

Defining more tables...

For concurrency, I'm deciding to use a simple global mutex around mutating operations plus DB transactions as a pragmatic single-process approach, keeping plan-version checks enforced to avoid most races. Now I'm thinking through how to structure the service layer given the large scope of this code.

I'll use pgx with a connection pool and a thin query interface that works for both direct calls and transactions, plus helper scan functions for loading models, prioritizing correctness over elegance. For ETA estimation, I'm working through the time model: collection start time based on current time or requested earliest time, adding handling minutes for home/clinic pickup, then calculating the haversine distance for the leg from origin to entry node.

For each stop I'll add dwell time for handling, and for each connection travel time between nodes, with final ETA being arrival at the lab plus lab processing time becoming the journey's estimated delivery. For home-origin entry node selection, I need multi-source Dijkstra across candidate collection points to find the one minimizing total time to a lab, with edges constrained by active connections and cold-chain capacity requirements where needed.

Intermediate nodes need hub or transfer functions while the destination needs lab and acceptance functions, though a lab can also act as an intermediate if it has transfer capability; for node-origin entries any active node works, and if the origin node is itself an accepting lab the journey has zero legs and just becomes a direct lab assignment.

For timing, I'll use Dijkstra to minimize ETA and compare against the deadline—if the minimum reachable time exceeds the deadline, the route is marked unreachable. For stop sequencing I'm working out how locationId should be assigned for the pickup stop, leaning toward using the entry node's id with the origin's coordinates so the handoff stop lines up correctly downstream.

Now I'm mapping out the leg assignments: origin to entry, entry to hub, hub to lab, and figuring out how to populate the first/middle/final transport assignment fields depending on whether there are one, two, or three legs in the route.

For handoff nodes, I'm reasoning through whether intermediate locations need explicit node assignments — deciding that entry node E is a true handoff point since the courier delivers there for another courier to pick up, while a collection point origin likely hands off directly to the first-leg courier without a separate node assignment, and presealed-at-node cases get an auto-accepted node assignment for the handler.

For presealed samples, I realize initiate_handoff requires a fromAssignmentId, so I need to generate an entry assignment per registrant type: a collection point gets a collection assignment already marked accepted/sealed, a node handler gets a node assignment in progress, and I'm working out what a courier's entry assignment should look like.

I'm also designing the handoff sequencing logic, assigning a numeric sequence to each assignment across the journey (collection=1, transport legs and node stops interleaved, lab=last) so that an adjacent handoff check simply verifies the target's sequence is one greater than the source's, while also flagging invalid holders like a lab team member stationed somewhere that isn't the accepting lab or a node handler whose location doesn't match the origin node.

Now I'm working out progress checks: a leg can only be marked picked_up if the prior assignment is complete (otherwise prior_leg_incomplete) and if the worker is actually the current holder (otherwise custody_required), with prior-assignment completion checked first. I'm also tracing through the collection-to-transport1 handoff once the collection assignment is sealed and marked completed.

For transport legs, I'm mapping out the progression from offered through accepted, at_pickup, picked_up, in_transit, arrived, to delivered, tying custody checks to picked_up and making handoff confirmation the trigger that auto-completes the sending assignment while recording delivered_at. I'm reasoning that a manual 'delivered' status should only be allowed once the worker no longer holds custody, ensuring handoff actually occurred before the leg can close out.

For node and lab assignments, I'm sketching a similar offered → accepted → in_progress → completed flow, gated by confirmed handoffs on both the incoming and outgoing sides. I'm now considering the edge case where a node has no assigned handler, which could stall the journey, and whether couriers should be allowed to hand off directly to each other at a node to bypass that gap.

For the lab receiver flow, I'm defining confirm_laboratory_receipt as something only the assigned lab worker can trigger once they're the custody holder, using receipt_not_ready for samples not yet handed off and custody_conflict for cases where someone else holds custody.

On journey status, I'll just use 'active' from creation rather than a separate 'planned' phase, with pending/inProgress distinguishing dispatcher states based on whether any assignment is completed or in-progress.

I also need a background deadline monitor running every 10 seconds that flags active samples past their delivery deadline as 'expired', marks the journey expired too, and cancels any unfinished assignments while releasing reservations.

Similarly, missed collection windows should trigger expiry with a 'collection_window_missed' reason, and offers expiring just trigger re-offering. For unassigned due items beyond the grace period, I'll flag an exception once ('no_qualified_worker') but keep retrying worker offers rather than halting the journey -- and if a worker later accepts, the sample can still proceed to collection and sealing even though the exception flag remains set on record.

Now I need to handle events (publishing on status changes, assignment offers, journey updates) and sort out requesterId rules in create_collection_request -- admins/dispatchers can set it explicitly, but requesters can only use their own ID or omit it. I also need to define handling_mismatch validation: container type must match the sample type's container type, and the requested temperature range must fall within the sample type's allowed range.

For the create request validation flow, I'm settling on an ordering: invalid_json, then invalid_origin for coordinate bounds, invalid_origin_type, invalid_time for unparsable timestamps, invalid_deadline when deadline precedes requestedAt, invalid_collection_window for window/deadline conflicts, not_found for missing sample type, handling_mismatch, and invalid_origin_state for inactive origin nodes. After validation passes, serviceability checks run separately -- if unserviceable, the request and sample still get created with a 201 response carrying an "unserviceable" status and reason.

409 errors like capacity_exhausted would only surface from race conditions after serviceability already approved capacity, since unserviceability itself is a valid 201 outcome. For defaults, earliestCollectionAt likely falls back to requestedAt and latestCollectionAt to the delivery deadline, since the response schema requires both fields populated.

I'm also wondering how the planner handles requestedAt values from fixed test fixtures that might sit in the past relative to real wall-clock time -- whether planning start should just be the later of now or earliestCollectionAt, and how that interacts with deadlines that may have already passed in fictional test timestamps.

I need error codes for collection outside the valid window too, plus similar invalid-time checks for handoff, confirmation, progress, checkpoint, exception, and receipt events — each validating against prior timestamps or future bounds. With that scoped out, I'm ready to start coding: Go backend first, then frontend, scripts, openapi.json, and README, starting with the module setup.

action.thought:
Design decisions (recorded for consistency while implementing):

DATASTORE: PostgreSQL only (durable, transactional, row locking for capacity). datastoresUsed=["postgresql"]. Opaque session tokens in a sessions table (survive restart).

BACKEND LAYOUT (Go, module "labsample"):
- cmd/server/main.go  (flags: -reset)
- internal/config, internal/db (schema.sql embedded, migrate, reset), internal/geo, internal/core (services), internal/httpapi (handlers + middleware), internal/realtime (events hub + ws).
- Single process-level mutex around mutating ops + DB transactions; PG serialization failure -> 409 concurrent_conflict.

ROLE/ASSIGNMENT MODEL:
- assignments: kind collection|transport|node|laboratory; sequence = global order in journey; leg_index for transport legs; sample_ids[] (batching), status: offered|accepted|at_pickup|picked_up|in_transit|arrived|delivered|in_progress|completed|cancelled|unassigned.
- Offer to one worker at a time; expiry -> treat as declined, re-offer. Fairness: exclude decliners, deprioritise >=3 declines in 30 min, then active count asc, last_offered_at asc.
- Collection with zero candidate users in system -> immediate sample exception reason no_qualified_worker; otherwise after grace for "due" assignments.

JOURNEY STRUCTURE: stops pickup(origin; locationId=entry node for home/clinic) -> handoff at entry node (home/clinic origins) -> handoff at intermediates -> delivery at lab. Transport legs between consecutive stops. Node assignment at each handoff stop; lab assignment at delivery.
- Replacement journeys: parent_journey_id, preserved_assignment_ids; old journey status replaced; sample.active_journey_id updated.
- plan_version incremented on every mutation; expectedPlanVersion mismatch -> stale_plan.

CUSTODY: handoff needs both confirmations; completion moves holder, completes from-assignment, starts to-assignment. Allow skipping an unassigned node assignment (courier-to-courier) for resilience.

ERRORS: {error, code} envelope; data wrapped as {data: ...}.

Extra UI helper endpoint: GET /api/ui/catalog (sample types + locations list) for forms — documented in openapi.json as UI helper. Everything else exactly per contract.

STATIC: serve frontend build from backend at /, map assets at /map-assets/ from MAP_ASSETS_DIR (default /opt/arena/map-assets).

action.file_text:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS settings (
    key   text PRIMARY KEY,
    value jsonb NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
    id                   uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    username             text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    password_hash        text NOT NULL,
    email                text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    full_name            text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    phone                text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    roles                text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    qualifications       text[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    certifications       jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
    active               boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    assigned_location_id uuid,
    available            boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    capacity_units       integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 5,
    last_offered_at      timestamptz,
    created_at           timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at           timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS users_roles_idx ON users USING gin (roles);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS users_assigned_location_idx ON users (assigned_location_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
    token        text PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    active_role  text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    last_seen_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS sessions_user_idx ON sessions (user_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS locations (
    id                    uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    name                  text NOT NULL,
    latitude              double precision NOT NULL,
    longitude             double precision NOT NULL,
    coverage_km           double precision NOT NULL DEFAULT 5,
    handling_minutes      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    active                boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    fn_collection_point   boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    fn_transfer_point     boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    fn_hub                boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    fn_laboratory         boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    capacity_units        integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    cooled_capacity_units integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at            timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at            timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS laboratory_acceptances (
    id             uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    laboratory_id  uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES locations (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    sample_type_id uuid NOT NULL,
    accepts        boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    updated_at     timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    UNIQUE (laboratory_id, sample_type_id)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS connections (
    id                    uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    from_location_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES locations (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    to_location_id        uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES locations (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    travel_minutes        integer NOT NULL,
    cost_units            double precision NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    cooled                boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    active                boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    capacity_units        integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    cooled_capacity_units integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at            timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at            timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS connections_from_idx ON connections (from_location_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS connections_to_idx ON connections (to_location_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sample_types (
    id                           uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    name                         text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    qualified_collector_required boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    required_qualification       text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    container_type               text NOT NULL,
    temperature_min_c            double precision NOT NULL,
    temperature_max_c            double precision NOT NULL,
    incompatible_sample_types    uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    requires_cooled_route        boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    batching_allowed             boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
    created_at                   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at                   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS collection_requests (
    id                        uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    requester_id              uuid NOT NULL,
    origin_latitude           double precision NOT NULL,
    origin_longitude          double precision NOT NULL,
    origin_type               text NOT NULL,
    origin_node_id            uuid,
    requested_at              timestamptz NOT NULL,
    delivery_deadline         timestamptz NOT NULL,
    earliest_collection_at    timestamptz NOT NULL,
    latest_collection_at      timestamptz NOT NULL,
    sample_type_id            uuid NOT NULL,
    container_type            text NOT NULL,
    temperature_min_c         double precision NOT NULL,
    temperature_max_c         double precision NOT NULL,
    incompatible_sample_types uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    serviceability            text NOT NULL,
    serviceability_reason     text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    target_laboratory_id      uuid,
    presealed                 boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    created_at                timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS collection_requests_requester_idx ON collection_requests (requester_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS samples (
    id                     uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    request_id             uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES collection_requests (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    status                 text NOT NULL,
    sealed                 boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
    sealed_at              timestamptz,
    collected_at           timestamptz,
    current_holder_id      uuid,
    active_journey_id      uuid,
    received_laboratory_id uuid,
    received_at            timestamptz,
    exception              jsonb,
    latest_latitude        double precision,
    latest_longitude       double precision,
    location_recorded_at   timestamptz,
    created_at             timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at             timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS samples_request_idx ON samples (request_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS samples_status_idx ON samples (status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS samples_holder_idx ON samples (current_holder_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS journeys (
    id                      uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    parent_journey_id       uuid,
    plan_version            integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    route_mode              text NOT NULL,
    status                  text NOT NULL,
    estimated_delivery_at   timestamptz,
    total_cost_units        double precision NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    target_laboratory_id    uuid,
    sample_ids              uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    replan_status           text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    replacement_journey_id  uuid,
    split_journey_id        uuid,
    preserved_assignment_ids uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    created_at              timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at              timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS journeys_status_idx ON journeys (status);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS journeys_samples_idx ON journeys USING gin (sample_ids);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS journey_stops (
    id            uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    journey_id    uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES journeys (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    location_id   uuid,
    stop_type     text NOT NULL,
    sequence      integer NOT NULL,
    estimated_at  timestamptz NOT NULL,
    dwell_minutes integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    latitude      double precision NOT NULL,
    longitude     double precision NOT NULL,
    sample_id     uuid,
    completed_at  timestamptz
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS journey_stops_journey_idx ON journey_stops (journey_id, sequence);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS assignments (
    id                     uuid PRIMARY KEY,
    journey_id             uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES journeys (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    sample_ids             uuid[] NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    kind                   text NOT NULL,
    sequence               integer NOT NULL,
    leg_index              integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    status                 text NOT NULL,
    worker_id              uuid,
    from_location_id       uuid,
    to_location_id         uuid,
    location_id            uuid,
    connection_id          uuid,
    from_latitude          double precision,
    from_longitude         double precision,
    to_latitude            double precision,
    to_longitude           double precision,
    required_qualification text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',

data.reasoning_content:
I'm designing the serviceability snapshot structure for core/network.go, including version tracking, locations, connections, and acceptance states, and working out how the network revision gets incremented on each mutation and used to refresh the snapshot.

For route planning, I'm figuring out capacity usage calculations from live reservations and the route-finding algorithm itself: a Dijkstra search over nodes by time, where edges come from active connections, allowing replanning from a given position, and terminating when an accepting active lab node is reached, while hub/transfer nodes can be passed through along the way.

Capacity checks require available units at each node and connection to meet demand, and I'm layering in relaxation flags (ignoring cooled requirements or capacity) to determine the reason behind routing decisions. I'm also working out the timing arithmetic—arrival and departure times based on travel and handling durations, with special cases for home versus node origins and when the entry point coincides with the destination lab.

For collection timing, I'm computing a start time bounded by the current time and earliest allowed, flagging anything past the latest collection deadline as unserviceable. I'm sketching out a routePlan struct to capture the path, connections, timestamps, cost, and first-mile duration needed to represent a full route.

Now I'm moving on to writing network.go, deciding I probably don't need exclusion params for locations or connections since disruptions already deactivate resources directly.

I'm thinking I can simplify by having loadUsage just call usageExcluding with a nil exclusion, and consolidate the duplicate logic later at compile time. I'm also spotting a subtlety in the Dijkstra deadline check — when an accepting lab is popped past its deadline but still has a hub/transfer, I continue expanding from it, which could miss a slower-but-valid path.

Sorting by depart time ends up equivalent to sorting by ETA for labs, so the min-heap ordering still holds, and skipping already-done nodes when pushing is fine. Moving on, I'm starting to sketch out the planning module that builds a journey from a route plan — creating stops, assignments, reservations, and offering logic — along with the journey creation function and its options struct.

Now I'm working through the stop generation logic: for origin at home/clinic, a pickup stop followed by handoff stops for intermediate path nodes and a delivery stop at the last node; for origin already at a node, pickup starts there instead, with the edge case of a single-node path producing both a pickup and delivery at the same lab. Then I'm starting on assignment sequencing, numbering them globally beginning with the collection assignment if applicable.

Now I'm mapping out transport legs between consecutive stops, tying each to its connection ID, cooling flag, and location, inserting node assignments after each handoff and a final laboratory assignment at the end, followed by reservations for cooled storage at each network node and per-sample-type units.

For connection reservations, I need to lock the relevant rows and check available capacity before confirming, returning a 409 if units exceed what's free. After assignments are created, I call the offering logic per assignment to try to find a worker, marking unassigned ones with a timestamp, and flagging collections with no eligible workers as exceptions. For presealed registrants, I'm auto-assigning based on their role—collection professionals get an in-progress assignment as both worker and sample holder, while delivery partners get accepted status on the first transport leg.

For node handlers, I'm validating that the origin is a node matching their assigned location, then creating an in-progress node assignment there before handoff to the transport courier. For laboratory team members, I check that their lab is the origin and accepts the sample type, creating an in-progress lab assignment; if the lab doesn't accept the type, I need to handle routing the sample elsewhere instead.

I'm now settling on initial sample statuses: non-presealed serviceable samples start as pending_collection, presealed ones as sealed, and unserviceable samples get flagged as unserviceable. Next I'm starting to sketch out planning.go, defining a journeyBuild struct and a buildJourney function that assembles the journey and assignments from the ordered sample IDs, requests, sample type, and route plan.

I'm also outlining helper functions for reserving capacity on a journey and offering assignments to the actor. For replanning that originates from a node rather than collection, I'm working through how the origin type, presealed flag, and node handler's existing assignment should chain into the new transport leg's handoff.

New assignment sequences must continue after the max sequence among preserved assignments, since loadJourneyAssignments includes those preserved entries for adjacency checks. For an in-transit replan where the courier is mid-leg to node N, I'm figuring out that the new journey should start with a handoff/node assignment at N rather than a pickup, since the courier will deliver to the node handler upon arrival.

For rendering, I'm renumbering the journey's legs by combining its own and preserved transport assignments, ordering them by sequence, and assigning clean leg indices since the original indices could otherwise collide.

I'm designing the HTTP layer before the services so their signatures align, having services take a context, actor, and raw JSON body and return a status, data, and error. This lets a generic handler wrapper manage auth, parsing, invocation, and response writing, plus an idempotency check for operations requiring a key. Writing handler wrapper code...

I'll go with a lenient JSON parsing approach that checks required fields rather than strictly rejecting unknown ones, and standardize responses as a data object on success or an error/code pair on failure. Now I'm planning out the service files: auth.go for authentication, session, and user management functions, and admin.go for location, connection, and capability configuration operations.

Continuing to organize core service files — requests.go for collection and ingestion flows, work.go for assignment and handoff operations, journeys.go for route planning and disruption handling, and views.go for read-side state rendering and search functions.

For the itor.go monitor file, I'm handling the background loop for offer expiry, deadlines, and grace periods. I'm planning helper functions to parse RFC3339 timestamp strings into time.Time values, returning an invalid_time error on failure, with separate handling for optional time fields.

For request validation, I'm decoding JSON into structs and catching type mismatches as invalid_json errors, checking required fields for zero values, and adding UUID validation since passing malformed UUID strings to pgx will trigger a database-level error that I need to map appropriately.

I realize a malformed UUID passed to pgx would produce a 500 rather than a clean error, so I'm deciding to validate UUID format upfront in each loader function and return a not-found response when the ID doesn't parse as a valid UUID. I'll patch the loaders in models.go with this check, then move on to writing auth.go.

data.reasoning_content:
Now I'm moving to the worker operations in work.go, the largest piece. I'm designing a shared helper to load an assignment for a worker, then working through AcceptAssignment: loading the assignment with a lock, returning 404 if missing, rejecting cancelled or completed assignments with a 409, and handling the case where it's already accepted or in-progress by the same worker.

For offers, I'm distinguishing between an assignment that was never offered versus one offered to someone else, checking role match, eligibility, availability, and offer expiration before marking it accepted and emitting the journey status update. Then I'm sketching DeclineAssignment similarly, requiring the assignment to be in offered status and owned by the current worker, with validation around the declined timestamp.

For the decline flow, I'm tracking who declined, logging the event, and re-offering to the next candidate if available. For UpdateAssignmentProgress, I'm enforcing worker ownership, valid status transitions by kind, timestamp ordering against the last progress update, and a strict transport sequence (accepted → at_pickup → picked_up → in_transit → arrived → delivered) where picked_up additionally requires the sample to be sealed and any prior sequential assignment to be complete.

For delivered, I'm working through the custody logic — the holder shouldn't be me at that point since it signals a confirmed handoff, so I need to reject marking delivered while I'm still holding it. I'm also deciding whether 'delivered' should count as a terminal state alongside 'completed' for the assignment-finished check, so finished assignments are detected consistently.

For non-transport assignments, I'll require accepted → in_progress → completed order, with completion for collection needing sealing plus handoff, for node needing handoff, and for laboratory needing receipt confirmation first. I also need to handle sample status side-effects like marking in_transit on pickup, and consider updating the sample's latest location on these transitions.

Now thinking about CollectAndSealSample: it needs to load the assignment with a lock, verify it's a collection-kind assignment tied to this sample (else return a not-found/mismatch error), then proceed to validation and sealing logic.

I'm mapping out the rejection cases: ownership checks on the worker, status-based rules for offered/cancelled/finished/already-sealed assignments (with idempotent return for an existing seal), sample state checks requiring pending_collection, certification/qualification checks, and timestamp validation for collectedAt against now, requestedAt, and the allowed collection window.

For successful compliance, I'm also handling container/temperature mismatches, updating the sample record (sealed status, holder, location, timestamps) and the assignment (in_progress, last_progress_at), flagging exceptions when non-compliant, writing audit log entries, and returning the final sealed response payload with compliance info.

Next I'm designing RecordWorkerLocation: validating the assignment and worker identity, coordinate/sequence/time formats, enforcing monotonic sequence and timestamp ordering against the last record (409 if stale), inserting the new location, updating any held samples' latest location, emitting a worker.location event, and returning a 201 with the recorded details. Then I start outlining RecordHandlingCheckpoint.

Now moving to InitiateHandoff: I need to lock the sample, verify the "from" assignment includes the sample and belongs to me with active status, confirm I'm still the current holder, and check no pending handoff already exists. For the "to" assignment, I'm validating it covers the sample, shares the journey (or a preserved chain), and that the receiver matches the worker on that assignment.

I also need to reject invalid receivers — self-handoffs, nonexistent users, unavailable receivers, or assignments not in an offerable state. Then I'm checking adjacency: the "to" assignment must directly follow "from" in sequence, or skip one unassigned node assignment (which gets cancelled), otherwise it's a nonadjacent handoff error. Finally, I'm validating route consistency between the from and to locations when the from assignment is a transport leg.

For the transport leg itself, I'll require its status be at least picked_up before allowing handoff, treating earlier states as an incomplete leg. If the from assignment is a collection, I require the sample be sealed, treating unsealed samples as a prior-leg-incomplete error, and I still need to validate that initiatedAt parses correctly and isn't too far in the future or predates sealing.

Now I'm working out ConfirmHandoff: validating the side is sender or receiver, locking the handoff record, handling cancelled/confirmed states appropriately (idempotent return on already-confirmed), checking the caller matches the expected side, and validating confirmedAt against initiatedAt.

Once both sides confirm, I need to transition custody to the receiver, mark the outgoing assignment finished with the right status per type (delivered for transport, completed for collection/node), move the incoming assignment to in_progress, update the sample's status and location based on the receiving kind, and release any reservations tied to the location or connection being vacated, plus mark relevant stops completed.

Next I'm designing ConfirmLaboratoryReceipt: verifying the actor's role and assigned location match the target lab, locking the sample row, handling idempotent/duplicate receipt confirmations, checking terminal states, and validating the lab location is active and properly functioning before proceeding.

I'm also working through holder and timing validation—requiring the current holder to match the confirming party, parsing receivedAt against sealed_at and deadline windows to catch invalid or late receipts, and resolving pending handoff conflicts before accepting the custody transfer.

For the accept-at-lab flow: once validations pass, I update the sample's received state, complete the lab assignment and journey, release reservations, close out the delivery stop, and emit audit/event records before returning the result.

Then for RecordLaboratoryException, I'm checking the operator's role and assigned location match, confirming the sample's journey targets this lab, and requiring the sample to actually be present (held by me or status at_laboratory) before allowing an exception to be logged.

Now I need to handle journey_inactive and invalid timestamp errors, then record the lab exception, update the sample to exception status with the reason, cancel remaining assignments, release reservations, and return the result. Time to start writing out work.go, which is going to be a long file.

thought.text: Now the journey management services: replanning, cancel, reroute, split, merge, edit, disruption.

data.reasoning_content:
I'm now working through journeys.go, focusing on the replanJourney helper: it checks whether the journey is active, loads the relevant data, and determines the status and any replacement journey needed for rerouting, splitting, merging, or disruption handling.

Then I'm reasoning through the position logic based on whether samples are sealed: if not sealed, it's a full replan including collection, preserving the collection assignment only if the worker is still eligible and available. If sealed with the collection professional still holding it, I set position to origin with collection skipped, preserving that assignment for handoff.

For in-progress transport legs, I set position to the leg's destination with FirstStopIsHandoff true, handling the edge case where the destination is already the lab by creating only a laboratory assignment instead of a redundant node assignment. I preserve all completed assignments plus the active leg, and similarly handle node handlers holding the sample at an in-progress node assignment by treating that node as the new origin.

For lab operators holding the sample, no replanning is needed since it's already at destination. For transport legs accepted but not yet picked up, I locate whichever assignment matches the current holder and is still active, then derive position based on its type — origin for collections, the node itself for node assignments, or not-required if already at a lab. Then I recompute the route excluding the removed journey, using the determined origin, current time, seal status, and the earliest sample deadline, marking the sample expired if no valid plan exists within the deadline.

If route planning fails for other reasons, I flag the sample as exception and mark the journey's replan status accordingly. Otherwise, I spin up a replacement journey linked back to the original, cancel any non-preserved unfinished assignments, release reservations, and update the journey and sample records to point to the new plan before offering out the new assignments.

I also need to verify that handoff logic correctly scopes the from/to assignments to the right journeys—preserved legs can reference the old journey while the active leg must belong to the current one—and that reservation releases during handoff completion correctly resolve to whichever journey actually holds the reservation. data.reasoning_content:
I'm planning to put split/merge/edit logic in a separate journeys_edit.go file, and need to fix buildJourney for FirstStopIsHandoff with a single-node lab path. For SplitJourney, I'm sketching out loading the journey for update, checking the version, and validating that the given sample IDs are a proper non-empty subset of the journey's samples before proceeding.

For each sample being split out, I need to check whether any transport assignment has already started—if so, that blocks the split since batched legs imply all samples share a vehicle. I also need to determine each sample's current position (at a node versus still at origin) by inspecting its collection assignment, then update the journey's sample list, remove or reassign other assignments, release reservations, and move the relevant collection assignments to a newly created journey that batches all the split samples together into one new journey as the contract expects.

For that new journey, I'm setting SkipCollection based on whether the moved collection assignment is unfinished or the sample is already sealed, giving the moved assignment a sequence of 0 so it precedes any newly created assignments; I also need to bump the version, set split_journey_id, adjust route_mode if the sample count dropped, and audit the result before returning both journeys. Now I'm sketching out the merge operation's signature, which takes a target journey, expected plan version, and a list of source journeys to combine.

For merging, I need to compare the remaining (incomplete) stop locations between target and sources — if both haven't started transport they're compatible, but a source with a completed leg forces a partial merge; sources still at the origin get pickup stops inserted ahead of existing pickups with renumbered sequences, and the first transport leg becomes a multi-pickup leg since its starting coordinates still work. I also need to append source sample IDs onto the target's transport/node/lab assignments and move source collection assignments into the target at sequence 0, though I'm now noticing a sequence collision risk between multiple zero-sequence collections and the target's own collection assignment given the adjacency check logic.

I realize the fix is to make collection-to-transport adjacency ignore assignments that don't belong to the same sample — filtering the "between" check by whether an assignment contains the sample's ID handles this cleanly, since per-sample collections only ever include their own sample. I should apply that same sample-filtering logic to the prior-assignment check used for detecting incomplete legs.

Now I'm mapping out the edit types: using replanJourney with an explicit path for add/remove/reorder/replace_route, handling replace_worker and reassign_worker in place, and mapping merge_samples/split_samples/split_batch/cancel_work/reroute to their corresponding merge/split/cancel/replan operations. I'm also working out how to compute the remaining path from a journey position — defining it as the sequence of network stop location IDs, carefully handling how pickup stops at node-origins versus home/clinic origins should be included.

For node origins where delivery is also at that node, buildJourney inserts an explicit delivery stop and I dedupe consecutive duplicates. Then I'm sketching the shapes for each change type: add_stop needs a location plus positioning info and dwell time, remove_stop just needs a stop or location id, reorder_stops takes an ordered list, replace_route takes a full explicit path, and reassign_worker needs the assignment and new worker ids, with merge_samples still to define.

For the response shape, I'm deciding the JourneyPlan returned for reroute/add/remove/reorder/replace_route should represent the original journey's plan with the replacementJourney embedded, since the plan schema's replacementJourney and replanStatus fields suggest the dispatcher wants visibility into both the original and its replacement rather than just the new plan.

For merge, I'll return the target plan; for replace_worker, the same journey's updated plan with a bumped version; for cancel_work, the cancelled plan.

Now I'm sketching out journeyPlanView, which builds the JourneyPlan map from the journey record -- computing fields like capacity used and available (treating capacityUsed as sample count and capacityAvailable as the minimum available units across the journey's resources), plus sample IDs, ordered stops, and legs.

For legs, assigned workers, and the various assignment IDs (collection, node, laboratory, transport), I'm deriving validity from the journey's active status, and including replan status, split journey, and a single level of recursive replacement journey info. For JourneyStop I'm including stop ID, location ID, stop type, sequence, estimated time, dwell minutes, coordinate, and completion time (supporting both camelCase and snake_case keys), and similarly for JourneyLeg I'm including assignment ID, sequence, status, and from-location.

I'm deciding legs should include all transport assignments from loadJourneyAssignments, including cancelled ones, ordered by sequence, so cancelled legs on replaced journeys stay informative. For a worker-scoped journey plan I'm limiting the data to their assigned legs and relevant stops, excluding unrelated details, while still including sample IDs tied to their assignments.

Now I'm turning to the requester-facing journey plan shape, which needs journey and parent IDs, plan version, route mode, status, delivery estimate, cost, sample IDs, ordered stops, and simplified leg objects without worker IDs — then I'll move on to sample views, role work, operations state, audit search, and bootstrap, starting with writing journeys_edit.go.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""End-to-end smoke test against a running application.

Usage: ADMIN_USERNAME=admin ADMIN_PASSWORD=... python3 scripts/e2e_smoke.py [base_url]

Walks the full lifecycle: network setup, users, serviceability dry run,
collection request, assignment offers, collection + sealing, custody handoffs,
laboratory receipt, replanning and audit search.
"""
import os
import sys
import uuid
import datetime as dt

import requests

BASE = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://127.0.0.1:8080"
API = BASE + "/api"
ADMIN_USER = os.environ.get("ADMIN_USERNAME", "admin")
ADMIN_PASS = os.environ.get("ADMIN_PASSWORD", "admin123")


def now(offset_minutes=0):
    return (dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc) + dt.timedelta(minutes=offset_minutes)).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ")


class Client:
    def __init__(self, token=None):
        self.token = token

    def call(self, path, body=None, method="POST", expect=None):
        headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.token}"} if self.token else {}
        if method == "POST":
            r = requests.post(f"{API}/{path}", json=body if body is not None else {}, headers=headers)
        else:
            r = requests.get(f"{API}/{path}", headers=headers)
        if expect is not None and r.status_code != expect:
            raise AssertionError(f"{method} {path} -> {r.status_code} {r.text} (expected {expect})")
        return r

    def data(self, path, body=None, expect=None, method="POST"):
        r = self.call(path, body, method=method, expect=expect)
        if r.status_code >= 400:
            raise AssertionError(f"{path}: {r.status_code} {r.text}")
        return r.json()["data"]


def login(username, password, role=None):
    r = requests.post(f"{API}/authenticate-user", json={"username": username, "password": password})
    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
    d = r.json()["data"]
    c = Client(d["sessionToken"])
    if role:
        c.data("select-active-role", {"role": role}, expect=200)
    return c, d


def main():
    print("== login admin")
    admin, info = login(ADMIN_USER, ADMIN_PASS)
    assert "administrator" in info["roles"]
    if info["activeRole"] != "administrator":
        admin.data("select-active-role", {"role": "administrator"})
    assert requests.get(BASE + "/ready").json() == {"status": "ready"}
    # invalid credentials
    r = requests.post(f"{API}/authenticate-user", json={"username": ADMIN_USER, "password": "nope"})
    assert r.status_code == 401 and r.json()["code"] == "invalid_credentials"

    hub = admin.data("create-location", {"name": f"Hub {tag}", "coordinate": {"latitude": 52.5300, "longitude": 13.4200}, "coverageKm": 3, "handlingMinutes": 10, "active": True, "functions": ["hub"]}, expect=201)
    lab = admin.data("create-location", {"name": f"Laboratory {tag}", "coordinate": {"latitude": 52.5400, "longitude": 13.4400}, "coverageKm": 2, "handlingMinutes": 5, "active": True, "functions": ["laboratory"]}, expect=201)
    for loc in (cp, hub, lab):
        admin.data("configure-capacity", {"resourceId": loc["locationId"], "capacityUnits": 10, "cooledCapacityUnits": 5}, expect=200)
    c1 = admin.data("create-connection", {"fromLocationId": cp["locationId"], "toLocationId": hub["locationId"], "travelMinutes": 20, "costUnits": 3, "cooled": True, "active": True}, expect=201)
    c2 = admin.data("create-connection", {"fromLocationId": hub["locationId"], "toLocationId": lab["locationId"], "travelMinutes": 25, "costUnits": 4, "cooled": True, "active": True}, expect=201)
    for c in (c1, c2):
        admin.data("configure-capacity", {"resourceId": c["connectionId"], "capacityUnits": 10, "cooledCapacityUnits": 5}, expect=200)
    catalog = admin.data("ui/catalog", method="GET")
    types = {t["name"]: t for t in catalog["sampleTypes"]}
    assert {"Amber", "Indigo", "Frost", "Pulse"} <= set(types), types.keys()
    amber = types["Amber"]
    for t in types.values():
        admin.data("configure-laboratory-acceptance", {"laboratoryId": lab["locationId"], "sampleTypeId": t["sampleTypeId"], "accepts": True}, expect=200)
    snap = admin.data("read-serviceability-snapshot", {})
    assert snap["status"] == "complete" and snap["activeCollectionPointCount"] >= 1

    print("== users")

    return (dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc) + dt.timedelta(minutes=offset_minutes)).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ")


class Client:
    def __init__(self, token=None):
        self.token = token

    def call(self, path, body=None, method="POST", expect=None):
        headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.token}"} if self.token else {}
        if method == "POST":

        else:

        if expect is not None and r.status_code != expect:
            raise AssertionError(f"{method} {path} -> {r.status_code} {r.text} (expected {expect})")

        r = self.call(path, body, method=method, expect=expect)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""End-to-end smoke test against a running application.

Usage: ADMIN_USERNAME=admin ADMIN_PASSWORD=... python3 scripts/e2e_smoke.py [base_url]

Walks the full lifecycle: network setup, users, serviceability dry run,
collection request, assignment offers, collection + sealing, custody handoffs,
laboratory receipt, replanning and audit search.
"""
import os
import sys
import uuid
import datetime as dt

import requests

BASE = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://127.0.0.1:8080"
API = BASE + "/api"
ADMIN_USER = os.environ.get("ADMIN_USERNAME", "admin")
ADMIN_PASS = os.environ.get("ADMIN_PASSWORD", "admin123")


def now(offset_minutes=0):
    return (dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc) + dt.timedelta(minutes=offset_minutes)).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ")


class Client:
    def __init__(self, token=None):
        self.token = token

    def call(self, path, body=None, method="POST", expect=None):
        headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.token}"} if self.token else {}
        if method == "POST":
            r = requests.post(f"{API}/{path}", json=body if body is not None else {}, headers=headers)
        else:
            r = requests.get(f"{API}/{path}", headers=headers)
        if expect is not None and r.status_code != expect:
            raise AssertionError(f"{method} {path} -> {r.status_code} {r.text} (expected {expect})")
        return r

    def data(self, path, body=None, expect=None, method="POST"):
        r = self.call(path, body, method=method, expect=expect)
        if r.status_code >= 400:
            raise AssertionError(f"{path}: {r.status_code} {r.text}")
        return r.json()["data"]


def login(username, password, role=None):
    r = requests.post(f"{API}/authenticate-user", json={"username": username, "password": password})
    assert r.status_code == 200, r.text
    d = r.json()["data"]
    c = Client(d["sessionToken"])
    if role:
        c.data("select-active-role", {"role": role}, expect=200)
    return c, d


def main():
    print("== login admin")
    admin, info = login(ADMIN_USER, ADMIN_PASS)
    assert "administrator" in info["roles"]
    if info["activeRole"] != "administrator":
        admin.data("select-active-role", {"role": "administrator"})
    assert requests.get(BASE + "/ready").json() == {"status": "ready"}
    # invalid credentials
    r = requests.post(f"{API}/authenticate-user", json={"username": ADMIN_USER, "password": "nope"})
    assert r.status_code == 401 and r.json()["code"] == "invalid_credentials"

    tag = uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]
    print("== network")
    cp = admin.data("create-location", {"name": f"Collection Centre {tag}", "coordinate": {"latitude": 52.5200, "longitude": 13.4050}, "coverageKm": 5, "handlingMinutes": 5, "active": True, "functions": ["collection_point", "transfer_point"]}, expect=201)
    hub = admin.data("create-location", {"name": f"Hub {tag}", "coordinate": {"latitude": 52.5300, "longitude": 13.4200}, "coverageKm": 3, "handlingMinutes": 10, "active": True, "functions": ["hub"]}, expect=201)
    lab = admin.data("create-location", {"name": f"Laboratory {tag}", "coordinate": {"latitude": 52.5400, "longitude": 13.4400}, "coverageKm": 2, "handlingMinutes": 5, "active": True, "functions": ["laboratory"]}, expect=201)
    for loc in (cp, hub, lab):
        admin.data("configure-capacity", {"resourceId": loc["locationId"], "capacityUnits": 10, "cooledCapacityUnits": 5}, expect=200)
    c1 = admin.data("create-connection", {"fromLocationId": cp["locationId"], "toLocationId": hub["locationId"], "travelMinutes": 20, "costUnits": 3, "cooled": True, "active": True}, expect=201)
    c2 = admin.data("create-connection", {"fromLocationId": hub["locationId"], "toLocationId": lab["locationId"], "travelMinutes": 25, "costUnits": 4, "cooled": True, "active": True}, expect=201)
    for c in (c1, c2):
        admin.data("configure-capacity", {"resourceId": c["connectionId"], "capacityUnits": 10, "cooledCapacityUnits": 5}, expect=200)
    catalog = admin.data("ui/catalog", method="GET")
    types = {t["name"]: t for t in catalog["sampleTypes"]}
    assert {"Amber", "Indigo", "Frost", "Pulse"} <= set(types), types.keys()
    amber = types["Amber"]
    for t in types.values():
        admin.data("configure-laboratory-acceptance", {"laboratoryId": lab["locationId"], "sampleTypeId": t["sampleTypeId"], "accepts": True}, expect=200)
    snap = admin.data("read-serviceability-snapshot", {})
    assert snap["status"] == "complete" and snap["activeCollectionPointCount"] >= 1

    print("== users")
    pw = "Passw0rd!"
    def mk(username, roles, **extra):
        body = {"username": username, "initialPassword": pw, "fullName": username, "roles": roles, "active": True}
        body.update(extra)
        return admin.data("create-user", body, expect=201)
    requester = mk(f"req_{tag}", ["requester"])
    collector = mk(f"col_{tag}", ["collection_professional"], qualifications=["amber"], certifications=[{"code": "amber", "active": True}])
    courier1 = mk(f"cour1_{tag}", ["delivery_partner"])
    courier2 = mk(f"cour2_{tag}", ["delivery_partner"])
    hubworker = mk(f"hub_{tag}", ["node_handler"], assignedLocationId=hub["locationId"])
    cpworker = mk(f"cp_{tag}", ["node_handler"], assignedLocationId=cp["locationId"])
    labworker = mk(f"lab_{tag}", ["laboratory_team", "requester"], assignedLocationId=lab["locationId"])
    r = admin.call("create-user", {"username": f"req_{tag}", "initialPassword": pw, "roles": ["requester"], "active": True})
    assert r.status_code == 409 and r.json()["code"] == "username_exists"

    print("== multi-role selection")
    labc, labinfo = login(labworker["username"], pw)
    assert labinfo["activeRole"] == "" and set(labinfo["roles"]) == {"laboratory_team", "requester"}
    r = labc.call("list-role-work", {})
    assert r.status_code == 409 and r.json()["code"] == "role_not_selected", r.text
    r = labc.call("select-active-role", {"role": "dispatcher"})
    assert r.status_code == 403 and r.json()["code"] == "role_not_held"
    sel = labc.data("select-active-role", {"role": "laboratory_team"}, expect=200)
    assert sel["activeRole"] == "laboratory_team" and set(sel["roles"]) == {"laboratory_team", "requester"}
    boot = labc.data("ui/bootstrap", method="GET")
    assert boot["user"]["activeRole"] == "laboratory_team" and boot["user"]["roleSelectionRequired"] is False

    print("== serviceability dry run")
    req, _ = login(requester["username"], pw, "requester")
    origin = {"latitude": 52.5215, "longitude": 13.4080}
    body = {"origin": origin, "originType": "home", "sampleTypeId": amber["sampleTypeId"], "requestedAt": now(), "deliveryDeadline": now(240)}
    sv = req.data("check-serviceability", body, expect=200)
    assert sv["serviceable"] is True and sv["reason"] == "serviceable" and sv["targetLaboratoryId"] == lab["locationId"], sv
    far = req.data("check-serviceability", dict(body, origin={"latitude": 53.9, "longitude": 10.0}), expect=200)
    assert far["serviceable"] is False and far["reason"] == "outside_service_coverage"
    late = req.data("check-serviceability", dict(body, deliveryDeadline=now(10)), expect=200)
    assert late["serviceable"] is False and late["reason"] == "deadline_unreachable", late
    r = req.call("check-serviceability", dict(body, deliveryDeadline=now(-10)))
    assert r.status_code == 400 and r.json()["code"] == "invalid_deadline"
    work = req.data("list-role-work", {})
    assert work["pending"] == [] and work["inProgress"] == [] and work["completed"] == []
    r = req.call("read-operations-state", {})
    assert r.status_code == 403

    print("== collection request")
    cr = req.data("create-collection-request", dict(body, containerType=amber["containerType"], temperatureMinC=amber["temperatureMinC"], temperatureMaxC=amber["temperatureMaxC"], earliestCollectionAt=now(-5), latestCollectionAt=now(90)), expect=201)
    assert cr["serviceability"] == "serviceable" and cr["journeyId"] and cr["activeAssignmentIds"], cr
    sample_id, journey_id = cr["sampleId"], cr["journeyId"]
    r = req.call("create-collection-request", dict(body, containerType="wrong", temperatureMinC=0, temperatureMaxC=1))
    assert r.status_code == 400 and r.json()["code"] == "handling_mismatch"
    state = req.data(f"read-sample-state/{sample_id}", method="GET")
    assert state["state"]["status"] == "pending_collection" and state["timeline"], state
    plan = req.data("read-journey-plan", {"journeyId": journey_id})
    assert plan["journeyId"] == journey_id and "workerId" not in (plan["legs"][0] if plan["legs"] else {})
    dplan = admin.data("read-journey-plan", {"journeyId": journey_id})
    assert dplan["routeMode"] == "multi_stop" and len(dplan["legs"]) == 2 and dplan["planVersion"] == 1, dplan
    assert [s["stopType"] for s in dplan["orderedStops"]] == ["pickup", "handoff", "handoff", "delivery"], dplan["orderedStops"]

    print("== collection")
    col, _ = login(collector["username"], pw, "collection_professional")
    work = col.data("list-role-work", {})
    assert len(work["pending"]) == 1 and work["pending"][0]["kind"] == "collection", work
    col_asg = work["pending"][0]["assignmentId"]
    r = col.call("collect-and-seal-sample", {"sampleId": sample_id, "assignmentId": col_asg, "collectedAt": now(), "containerType": amber["containerType"], "observedTemperatureC": amber["temperatureMinC"], "idempotencyKey": "k0"})
    assert r.status_code == 409 and r.json()["code"] == "collection_not_ready", r.text
    r = col.call("accept-assignment", {"assignmentId": col_asg})
    assert r.status_code == 400 and r.json()["code"] == "idempotency_required"
    acc = col.data("accept-assignment", {"assignmentId": col_asg, "idempotencyKey": f"acc-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    assert acc["status"] == "accepted"
    acc2 = col.data("accept-assignment", {"assignmentId": col_asg, "idempotencyKey": f"acc-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    assert acc2 == acc
    r = col.call("accept-assignment", {"assignmentId": col_asg, "idempotencyKey": f"acc-{tag}"}, )
    r = col.call("accept-assignment", {"assignmentId": col_asg, "idempotencyKey": f"acc-{tag}-other"})
    assert r.status_code == 201  # already mine
    col.data("record-worker-location", {"assignmentId": col_asg, "coordinate": origin, "sequence": 1, "recordedAt": now()}, expect=201)
    r = col.call("record-worker-location", {"assignmentId": col_asg, "coordinate": origin, "sequence": 1, "recordedAt": now()})
    assert r.status_code == 409 and r.json()["code"] == "stale_location"
    sealed = col.data("collect-and-seal-sample", {"sampleId": sample_id, "assignmentId": col_asg, "collectedAt": now(), "containerType": amber["containerType"], "observedTemperatureC": amber["temperatureMinC"], "idempotencyKey": f"seal-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    assert sealed["status"] == "sealed" and sealed["currentHolderId"] == collector["userId"] and sealed["handlingCompliant"] is True
    life = req.data("read-sample-lifecycle", {"sampleId": sample_id})
    assert life["sealed"] is True and life["currentHolderId"] == collector["userId"] and life["status"] == "sealed"

    print("== first transport leg")
    legs = admin.data("read-journey-plan", {"journeyId": journey_id})["legs"]
    leg1, leg2 = legs[0], legs[1]
    # whoever got the offer accepts it
    def worker_for(leg):
        return leg.get("workerId")
    def courier_client(worker_id):
        name = courier1["username"] if worker_id == courier1["userId"] else courier2["username"]
        return login(name, pw, "delivery_partner")[0]
    w1 = worker_for(leg1)
    assert w1 in (courier1["userId"], courier2["userId"]), leg1
    cour = courier_client(w1)
    other = courier_client(courier2["userId"] if w1 == courier1["userId"] else courier1["userId"])
    r = other.call("accept-assignment", {"assignmentId": leg1["assignmentId"], "idempotencyKey": "x"})
    assert r.status_code == 409 and r.json()["code"] == "offer_not_offered", r.text
    cour.data("accept-assignment", {"assignmentId": leg1["assignmentId"], "idempotencyKey": f"acc1-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    r = cour.call("update-assignment-progress", {"assignmentId": leg1["assignmentId"], "status": "picked_up", "occurredAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"pu-early-{tag}"})
    assert r.status_code == 409 and r.json()["code"] == "custody_required", r.text
    # collector hands off to the courier
    h = col.data("initiate-handoff", {"sampleId": sample_id, "fromAssignmentId": col_asg, "toAssignmentId": leg1["assignmentId"], "receiverId": w1, "initiatedAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"h1-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    assert h["status"] == "pending" and h["currentHolderId"] == collector["userId"]
    c = col.data("confirm-handoff", {"handoffId": h["handoffId"], "confirmationSide": "sender", "confirmedAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"h1s-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    assert c["status"] == "pending" and c["currentHolderId"] == collector["userId"]
    c = cour.data("confirm-handoff", {"handoffId": h["handoffId"], "confirmationSide": "receiver", "confirmedAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"h1r-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    assert c["status"] == "confirmed" and c["currentHolderId"] == w1
    c2 = cour.data("confirm-handoff", {"handoffId": h["handoffId"], "confirmationSide": "receiver", "confirmedAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"h1r2-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    assert c2["currentHolderId"] == w1  # no duplicate transfer
    cour.data("update-assignment-progress", {"assignmentId": leg1["assignmentId"], "status": "in_transit", "occurredAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"it-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    cour.data("record-worker-location", {"assignmentId": leg1["assignmentId"], "coordinate": {"latitude": 52.525, "longitude": 13.41}, "sequence": 1, "recordedAt": now()}, expect=201)
    cour.data("update-assignment-progress", {"assignmentId": leg1["assignmentId"], "status": "arrived", "occurredAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"arr-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    st = admin.data(f"read-sample-state/{sample_id}", method="GET")
    assert st["state"]["status"] == "in_transit" and st["locationStale"] is False

    print("== hub handling")
    hubc, _ = login(hubworker["username"], pw, "node_handler")
    hw = hubc.data("list-role-work", {})
    assert len(hw["pending"]) == 1 and hw["pending"][0]["kind"] == "node", hw
    node_asg = hw["pending"][0]["assignmentId"]
    hubc.data("accept-assignment", {"assignmentId": node_asg, "idempotencyKey": f"hub-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    cap = hubc.data("read-operations-state", {}) if False else None
    h2 = cour.data("initiate-handoff", {"sampleId": sample_id, "fromAssignmentId": leg1["assignmentId"], "toAssignmentId": node_asg, "receiverId": hubworker["userId"], "initiatedAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"h2-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    hubc.data("confirm-handoff", {"handoffId": h2["handoffId"], "confirmationSide": "receiver", "confirmedAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"h2r-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    c = cour.data("confirm-handoff", {"handoffId": h2["handoffId"], "confirmationSide": "sender", "confirmedAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"h2s-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    assert c["status"] == "confirmed" and c["currentHolderId"] == hubworker["userId"]
    cp_ = hubc.data("record-handling-checkpoint", {"sampleId": sample_id, "assignmentId": node_asg, "locationId": hub["locationId"], "containerType": amber["containerType"], "observedTemperatureC": amber["temperatureMaxC"], "recordedAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"cp-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    assert cp_["compliant"] is True and cp_["sampleStatus"] == "at_node"
    hubcap = hubc.data("configure-capacity", {"resourceId": hub["locationId"], "capacityUnits": 12, "cooledCapacityUnits": 5}, expect=200)
    assert hubcap["capacityUnits"] == 12
    r = hubc.call("configure-capacity", {"resourceId": lab["locationId"], "capacityUnits": 12})
    assert r.status_code == 403
    cour_work = cour.data("list-role-work", {})
    assert any(i["assignmentId"] == leg1["assignmentId"] for i in cour_work["completed"]), cour_work

    print("== final leg + laboratory receipt")
    legs = admin.data("read-journey-plan", {"journeyId": journey_id})["legs"]
    leg2 = legs[1]
    w2 = leg2["workerId"]
    cour2 = courier_client(w2)
    cour2.data("accept-assignment", {"assignmentId": leg2["assignmentId"], "idempotencyKey": f"acc2-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    h3 = hubc.data("initiate-handoff", {"sampleId": sample_id, "fromAssignmentId": node_asg, "toAssignmentId": leg2["assignmentId"], "receiverId": w2, "initiatedAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"h3-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    hubc.data("confirm-handoff", {"handoffId": h3["handoffId"], "confirmationSide": "sender", "confirmedAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"h3s-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    cour2.data("confirm-handoff", {"handoffId": h3["handoffId"], "confirmationSide": "receiver", "confirmedAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"h3r-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    cour2.data("update-assignment-progress", {"assignmentId": leg2["assignmentId"], "status": "arrived", "occurredAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"arr2-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    lw = labc.data("list-role-work", {})
    assert len(lw["pending"]) == 1 and lw["pending"][0]["kind"] == "laboratory", lw
    lab_asg = lw["pending"][0]["assignmentId"]
    labc.data("accept-assignment", {"assignmentId": lab_asg, "idempotencyKey": f"lab-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    r = labc.call("confirm-laboratory-receipt", {"sampleId": sample_id, "laboratoryId": lab["locationId"], "receivedAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"rc-early-{tag}"})
    assert r.status_code == 409 and r.json()["code"] == "receipt_not_ready", r.text
    h4 = cour2.data("initiate-handoff", {"sampleId": sample_id, "fromAssignmentId": leg2["assignmentId"], "toAssignmentId": lab_asg, "receiverId": labworker["userId"], "initiatedAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"h4-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    cour2.data("confirm-handoff", {"handoffId": h4["handoffId"], "confirmationSide": "sender", "confirmedAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"h4s-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    labc.data("confirm-handoff", {"handoffId": h4["handoffId"], "confirmationSide": "receiver", "confirmedAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"h4r-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    rc = labc.data("confirm-laboratory-receipt", {"sampleId": sample_id, "laboratoryId": lab["locationId"], "receivedAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"rc-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    assert rc["status"] == "received"
    life = req.data("read-sample-lifecycle", {"sampleId": sample_id})
    assert life["status"] == "received" and len(life["completedLegIds"]) == 2, life
    plan = admin.data("read-journey-plan", {"journeyId": journey_id})
    assert plan["status"] == "completed", plan["status"]
    rw = req.data("list-role-work", {})
    assert len(rw["completed"]) == 1
    statuses = [e["action"] for e in life["timeline"] if e["action"].startswith("sample.status.")]
    assert statuses[0] == "sample.status.pending_collection" and statuses[-1] == "sample.status.received", statuses

    print("== audit")
    audit = admin.data("search-audit-trail", {"entityId": sample_id, "limit": 50, "order": "oldest_first"})
    assert audit["total"] >= 5 and audit["entries"][0]["actorRole"] and audit["order"] == "oldest_first"
    audit2 = admin.data("search-audit-trail", {"query": "custody", "limit": 5})
    assert audit2["returned"] <= 5 and all("custody" in e["action"] for e in audit2["entries"]), audit2
    logins = admin.data("search-audit-trail", {"action": "auth.login", "success": False})
    assert logins["total"] >= 1

    print("== operations + disruption/replan")
    cr2 = req.data("create-collection-request", dict(body, containerType=amber["containerType"], temperatureMinC=amber["temperatureMinC"], temperatureMaxC=amber["temperatureMaxC"]), expect=201)
    j2 = cr2["journeyId"]
    ops = admin.data("read-operations-state", {})
    assert any(s["sampleId"] == cr2["sampleId"] for s in ops["samples"]) and ops["workers"] and ops["locations"]
    plan2 = admin.data("read-journey-plan", {"journeyId": j2})
    r = admin.call("reroute-journey", {"journeyId": j2, "expectedPlanVersion": 99, "idempotencyKey": f"rr0-{tag}"})
    assert r.status_code == 409 and r.json()["code"] == "stale_plan"
    # Add an alternate path cp -> lab so the hub can be disrupted.
    c3 = admin.data("create-connection", {"fromLocationId": cp["locationId"], "toLocationId": lab["locationId"], "travelMinutes": 60, "costUnits": 9, "cooled": False, "active": True}, expect=201)
    admin.data("configure-capacity", {"resourceId": c3["connectionId"], "capacityUnits": 10, "cooledCapacityUnits": 0}, expect=200)
    dis = admin.data("report-disruption", {"resourceType": "node", "resourceId": hub["locationId"], "reason": "power outage", "occurredAt": now(), "idempotencyKey": f"dis-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    assert cr2["sampleId"] in dis["affectedSampleIds"] and dis["replanStatus"] == "replaced", dis
    old = admin.data("read-journey-plan", {"journeyId": j2})
    assert old["status"] == "replaced" and old["replacementJourney"]["status"] == "active", old["status"]
    new_plan = old["replacementJourney"]
    assert len(new_plan["legs"]) == 1 and new_plan["parentJourneyId"] == j2
    st2 = req.data(f"read-sample-state/{cr2['sampleId']}", method="GET")
    assert st2["activeJourneyId"] == new_plan["journeyId"]
    admin.data("set-location-status", {"locationId": hub["locationId"], "active": True}, expect=200)
    canc = admin.data("cancel-journey", {"journeyId": new_plan["journeyId"], "expectedPlanVersion": new_plan["planVersion"], "reason": "test", "idempotencyKey": f"can-{tag}"}, expect=201)
    assert canc["status"] == "cancelled"

    print("== presealed ingest at node")
    cpc, _ = login(cpworker["username"], pw, "node_handler")
    ps = cpc.data("ingest-presealed-sample", {"origin": {"latitude": 52.52, "longitude": 13.405}, "originType": "node", "originNodeId": cp["locationId"], "sampleTypeId": amber["sampleTypeId"], "requestedAt": now(), "deliveryDeadline": now(300), "containerType": amber["containerType"], "temperatureMinC": amber["temperatureMinC"], "temperatureMaxC": amber["temperatureMaxC"]}, expect=201)
    assert ps["alreadySealed"] is True and ps["serviceability"] == "serviceable", ps
    psl = cpc.data("read-sample-lifecycle", {"sampleId": ps["sampleId"]})
    assert psl["sealed"] is True and psl["currentHolderId"] == cpworker["userId"]
    psplan = admin.data("read-journey-plan", {"journeyId": ps["journeyId"]})
    assert psplan["collectionAssignmentIds"] == [] and psplan["nodeAssignmentIds"], psplan

    print("== frost requires cooled route; pulse cannot batch")
    frost = types["Frost"]
    r = req.data("check-serviceability", dict(body, sampleTypeId=frost["sampleTypeId"]), expect=200)
    assert r["serviceable"] is True, r
    admin.data("set-connection-status", {"connectionId": c2["connectionId"], "active": False}, expect=200)
    r = req.data("check-serviceability", dict(body, sampleTypeId=frost["sampleTypeId"]), expect=200)
    assert r["serviceable"] is False and r["reason"] == "no_route", r
    admin.data("set-connection-status", {"connectionId": c2["connectionId"], "active": True}, expect=200)

    print("== events")
    ev = admin.call("events?since=0", method="GET", expect=200).json()["data"]
    assert ev["events"] and ev["cursor"] >= ev["events"][-1]["id"]
    print("ALL OK")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
